newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends firm on consumption ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends firm on consumption ideas.

text.p: CBOT rice futures closed firm despite a hike by USDA in its production estimate for the 1996 U.S. rice crop, traders said.
"There is good demand under the market so it is holding up okay," a trader said.
Technicals also indicate November should hold in a range from $9.65 per cwt to $9.85, traders said.
"We successfullly tested the $9.65 level this week and it was refused (support held)," he said. "It's significant we had an outside up week."
Prospects for rice demand kept the market from falling.

USDA early Friday said 1996 U.S. rice production would total 176.1 million cwt, up from the September outlook for 171.5 million. But the government also increased to 74.0 million cwt from the previous 72.0 million its forecast for U.S. rice exports.
"It's good quality long grain and there will continue to be good demand for top quality rice," he said.
Rice closed unchnged to five cents per cwt higher, with November up five at $9.85 per cwt. January was up 3-1/2 cents at $9.92-1/2 and new crop September closed two cents higher at $10.01 per cwt.
Traders said there continues to be fair activity, producer hedging and long hedges by consumers in the September contract.

The hike in rice output stemmed partly from an increase by USDA in its forecast for 1996 rice harvested acreage to 2.91 million from the previous 2.88 million. The government also increased its estimate for yield per acre to 6,053 lbs per acre from the previous 5,957 lbs.
U.S. rice ending stocks were pegged by the government at 27.7 million cwt from the previous 25.4 million.
Rice futures volume was estimated at 200 contracts, down from 299 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Rice options volume was estimated at 30 contracts, below the 41 contracts traded Thursday.
